aspects.says: The host's own echo matches no waiting request; without a request listener that answers it through its source, it ends on the unhandled queue and the host drops the link.
basis: section:11.6 The Host's Own Echo Is a Request, and Someone Must Answer It

aspects.says: A host that wants a sign-on declines or drops traffic on a new connection until it gets one, while isConnected() is already true.
basis: section:11.1 A Connected Link Is Not a Signed-On Link

aspects.says: At a planned stop the link leaves service before the 002, the 002 goes only to the connection that signed on, and the session is forgotten whatever the host answered.
basis: section:11.5 Take a Link Out of Service Before You Sign It Off

aspects.says: An enabled mark that is not the ready object, such as Boolean.TRUE, never matches, so the pool never uses the link.
basis: section:11.4 A Pool Uses a Link Only While It Is Signed On

aspects.says: The sign-on manager is a QBean deployed after the channels and QMUXes it names, configured through properties.
basis: section:11.3 A Sign-On Belongs to One Connection
aspects.reason: deployment order and properties are configuration that only a running Q2 shows; a practice would retype the descriptor

aspects.says: Adaptor and TCP keep-alives are answered below the host application, so only an expired echo shows that the host stopped answering.
basis: section:11.2 Only an Echo Proves the Host Is Answering

aspects.says: With check-enabled a pool uses a link only while its enabled mark is the very ready object, so a client without a pool must make the same identity check before it sends.
basis: section:11.4 A Pool Uses a Link Only While It Is Signed On

aspects.says: A sign-on belongs to the connection whose ready object it stored; comparing that object by identity catches every reconnect, while a boolean flag misses one that happened while the loop was busy.
basis: section:11.3 A Sign-On Belongs to One Connection
